newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat European car sales up 15 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: Fiat European car sales up 15 pct in August.

text.p: Italy's Fiat Auto said its car sales rose 15.2 percent in August in a European car market, excluding Italy, which rose just 6.1 percent.

Data on new Italian car registrations in August published on Tuesday showed Fiat group new registrations fell 12.96 percent on the same month last year to 31,040 while its market share slipped to 41.94 percent from 44.57 percent.
Fiat said in a statement that the drop in domestic sales last month was affected by the absence of any Fiat D sector - medium to large size - marques.
But this will be remedied with the launch on September 14 of the new Marea and Marea "weekend" station-wagon which will replace the ageing Tempra, Tempra SW and Croma models.
In the first eight months of this year, the European market - excluding Italy - posted a rise of 7.1 percent while Fiat group sales sawe an increase of 22.6 percent.

In August, Fiat Auto increased sales in Germany by 14.6 percent in a market which grew by 7.0 percent. In France, Fiat sales jumped 50 percent in a market which rose by 28.9 percent, and in Britain by 20.9 percent in a market which grew by only 1.8 percent.
